title: Post-Clearance Audit (PCA) and Enforcement
summary: The framework for post-clearance audits has transitioned from basic penalty clauses to a structured, risk-based management system. It now includes detailed procedural manuals for audit selection, notification, hearing, and recovery of underpaid taxes, aligning with the Customs Act, 2023.

evolution.methodology: Shifted from reactive penalty imposition to proactive risk-based audit cycles.
evolution.legal_basis: Transitioned from Customs Act, 1969 to Customs Act, 2023.

timeline.change: Initial provisions for penalties and license cancellation for non-compliance.
Formalized comprehensive audit manual, risk-based selection, and standardized recovery notices (Section 83A).
Updated penalty references to Customs Act, 2023 and formalized re-assessment procedures.

Customs Agent: A Customs Agent is subject to license cancellation and financial penalties for various infractions, including duty evasion, submission of fraudulent documents, or non-compliance with licensing conditions.
The Licensing Authority must provide the agent an opportunity to show cause within a specified period before taking any punitive action against their license or imposing a fine.
Penalties are tiered based on the nature of the offence, with specific scales for non-revenue related infractions, attempted revenue evasion, and actual revenue evasion.
Legal or administrative actions against a Customs Agent may be stayed if there is a pending case or claim under specified sub-rules until the matter is finalized.
Licensing Authority: The Licensing Authority is empowered to cancel the license of a Customs Agent and impose monetary penalties for breaches of customs regulations, professional negligence, or misconduct.
They are required to follow due process, including issuing a show-cause notice, before finalizing any cancellation or financial penalty.
Customs Duty: Failure to pay or evasion of Customs Duty by a Customs Agent, or failure to disclose information regarding a client's evasion of such taxes, constitutes grounds for license cancellation and penalty.
Financial penalties for customs-related offences are calculated based on the quantum of duty evasion or fixed minimum thresholds, depending on the severity and nature of the violation.

৪.১.১ অডিটের জন্য ব্যক্তি/প্রতিষ্ঠান নির্বাচন ও অডিট বাস্তবায়নকারী দপ্তরসমূহ—কাস্টমস রিস্ক ম্যানেজমেন্ট কমিশনারেট নিজস্ব রিস্ক ম্যানেজমেন্ট সফটওয়্যারের মাধ্যমে স্বয়ংক্রিয় কম্পিউটারাইজড পদ্ধতিতে বা সুনির্দিষ্ট অভিযোগ বা তথ্যের ভিত্তিতে পোস্ট ক্লিয়ারেন্স অডিটের জন্য সূচক নির্ধারণের পাশাপাশি প্রতিষ্ঠান বা পণ্য চালান নির্বাচন করবেন। কাস্টমস রিস্ক ম্যানেজমেন্ট কমিশনারেট নির্বাচিত প্রতিষ্ঠান সিস্টেম বেইজড পিসিএ কার্যক্রম সম্পন্ন করার জন্য শুল্ক মূল্যায়ন ও অভ্যন্তরীণ নিরীক্ষা কমিশনারেটে প্রেরণ করবেন এবং নির্বাচিত বিল অব এন্ট্রি/চালান ট্র্যানজ্যাকশন বেইজড পিসিএ কার্যক্রম সম্পন্ন করার জন্য সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টম হাউস বা কমিশনারেট এ প্রেরণ করবেন।

শুল্ক মূল্যায়ন ও অভ্যন্তরীণ নিরীক্ষা কমিশনারেট সকল সিস্টেম বেইজড অডিট পরিচালনা করবেন; তবে, প্রয়োজনে অডিট কার্যক্রম পরিচালনার জন্য বিভিন্ন কাস্টম হাউস বা কমিশনারেট এবং/অথবা কাস্টমস গোয়েন্দা ও তদন্ত পরিদপ্তর থেকে প্রয়োজনীয় সংখ্যক কর্মকর্তা অডিট কমিটিতে অন্তর্ভুক্ত করতে পারবেন। সিস্টেম বেইজড অডিটের ক্ষেত্রে অডিট পরবর্তী সকল কার্যক্রম যেমনঃ শুল্ক-করাদি নিরূপণ, প্রযোজ্য ক্ষেত্রে জরিমানা আরোপ, কারণ দর্শানো নোটিশ, দাবীনামা জারী, বকেয়া রাজস্ব আদায় ও প্রয়োজনীয় আইনগত পদক্ষেপসমূহ স্ব স্ব কাস্টম হাউস কর্তৃক পরিচালিত হবে। শুল্ক মূল্যায়ন ও অভ্যন্তরীণ নিরীক্ষা কমিশনারেট, কাস্টমস রিস্ক ম্যানেজমেন্ট কমিশনারেট এর নির্ধারিত প্রতিষ্ঠানের পাশাপাশি তাদের নিজস্ব রিস্ক ম্যানেজমেন্ট এর আওতায় নির্বাচিত প্রতিষ্ঠানের সিস্টেম বেইজড PCA এবং পণ্যচালানের ক্ষেত্রে ট্র্যানজ্যাকশন বেইজড অডিট সম্পাদন করিতে পারিবেন। কাস্টম হাউস/কাস্টমস স্টেশন, কাস্টমস রিস্ক ম্যানেজমেন্ট কমিশনারেট এর নির্ধারিত পণ্যচালানের পাশাপাশি তাদের নিজস্ব রিস্ক ম্যানেজমেন্ট এর আওতায় নির্বাচিত পণ্য চালানের ট্র্যানজ্যাকশন বেইজড PCA সম্পাদন করবেন।

Customs Risk Management Commissionerate: This office is responsible for selecting individuals and entities for Post Clearance Audit using both automated risk management software and specific intelligence or complaints.
It acts as the central hub for determining audit indicators and forwarding selected cases to the appropriate customs authority for further audit processing.
Post Clearance Audit: Post Clearance Audit is categorized into system-based audits and transaction-based audits to ensure compliance after the clearance of goods.
The audit process involves risk-based selection of entities and specific consignments for subsequent examination and revenue verification.
Customs Valuation and Internal Audit Com: This authority is tasked with conducting all system-based audits and has the power to form audit committees that may include officers from various custom houses or the Customs Intelligence and Investigation Directorate.
Beyond cases referred by the Customs Risk Management Commissionerate, this office may initiate its own system-based and transaction-based audits based on independent risk assessments.
Customs House: Custom Houses are responsible for the legal and administrative follow-up of system-based audits, including the determination of duties and taxes, issuance of show-cause notices, and recovery of outstanding revenue.

Each Custom House also performs transaction-based audit activities for selected consignments, either as designated by the Customs Risk Management Commissionerate or through its own internal risk management processes.
Customs Intelligence and Investigation D: Officers from this directorate may be included in audit committees to assist the Customs Valuation and Internal Audit Commissionerate in carrying out audit activities when necessary.

Customs Audit: The audit process involves identifying additional duty and tax liabilities that must be formally communicated to the entity under audit.

Upon completion of an audit, an internal management report must be generated to summarize the findings, highlight key risk indicators for preventive measures, and share the results with relevant internal stakeholders.
Following the submission of the final report, any unnecessary documents provided by the auditee must be returned, and internal records must be properly filed and returned to the respective offices.
Customs Duty and Taxes: Entities found liable for additional duty and taxes during an audit are required to pay the assessed amounts within a specified timeframe.

Customs Audit Manual: This manual establishes the framework, methodologies, and operational instructions for conducting post-clearance audits to ensure efficiency and effectiveness.
It aims to standardize audit procedures, provide clear guidance to customs officials on risk-based selection, planning, and reporting, and ensure professional conduct across all audit activities.
Customs Officials: The manual provides customs officials with clear instructions for every stage of the audit process, including risk assessment, selection of entities for audit, audit planning, fieldwork, and report generation.
Risk Management: The manual mandates the proper application of risk management techniques to ensure audits are conducted fairly, professionally, and consistently across all business entities.
Customs Duty and Taxes: A primary objective of the audit process is to prevent procedural lapses during the recovery of evaded duties and taxes, ensuring that such recovery is accurate and systematic.

Customs Duty: Audit procedures must prioritize verifying the ratio of finished goods produced against total imported inputs to ensure that all relevant duties and taxes have been correctly calculated and paid.

Customs Duty and Taxes Recovery: This standing order prescribes the operational steps for customs officials to recover unpaid or underpaid duties and taxes from importers. The process follows a structured sequence of administrative actions to ensure legal compliance and fairness.
Show Cause Notice: Under the first step of the recovery procedure, customs officers are required to issue a show cause notice to the importer pursuant to the relevant provisions of the Customs Act regarding the unpaid duty amount. This document serves as the formal initiation of the recovery process as outlined in the specified appendix.
Importer: The importer must be issued a show cause notice and subsequently provided with an opportunity for a hearing to address the claims of unpaid or underpaid duties. Following a review of the facts, if the liability is proven, the importer is formally served with a demand notice for the settlement of the customs duties and taxes.
Demand Notice: Once a hearing has been conducted and the underpayment of duties is established, a formal demand notice is issued to the importer as the final step in the recovery process. This notice requires the importer to settle the outstanding customs duties and taxes in accordance with the established legal procedures.

member_objects.clause_title: CUSTOMS ACT, 1969 এর SECTION 83A এর অধীন কারণ দর্শানো নোটিশের নমুনা

Customs Act 1969: This act provides the legal framework under Section 83A for issuing show cause notices regarding the recovery of short-paid customs duties and taxes.
The act empowers customs officials to initiate proceedings for the recovery of dues based on evidence available on file if a formal response is not received within the specified timeframe.
Bangladesh Customs Tariff: The tariff schedule, along with other relevant laws and explanatory notes, serves as the basis for post-clearance audit reviews conducted by customs authorities to verify the correctness of duty and tax assessments.
World Customs Organization: The Explanatory Notes issued by this organization are utilized by customs authorities during post-clearance audits to support the classification and duty assessment of imported goods.
Customs Duty: The recovery process for short-paid duties and taxes is triggered when an importer receives duty-free benefits under an SRO for goods that are later determined to be ineligible for such exemptions.

Customs Act 1969: This instrument provides the legal framework for determining customs duties and taxes, specifically citing Section 32(4) for conducting hearings regarding misdeclared imports.
Section 32(1) identifies misdeclaration of goods as an offence, while Section 156 Table-1 Clause-14 prescribes the corresponding penalties for such violations.
Section 32(2) outlines the procedure for issuing show-cause notices when underpayment of customs duties and taxes is identified.
The Act grants the customs authority the power to finalize proceedings based on available evidence if the importer or their representative fails to attend the scheduled personal hearing.
Bangladesh Customs Tariff: The classification and duty assessment for imported goods are reviewed against the Bangladesh Customs Tariff during post-clearance audits.
World Customs Organization: Explanatory Notes issued by the World Customs Organization are utilized as a technical reference during the audit and valuation of imported goods.
Customs Authority: The customs authority is responsible for conducting post-clearance audits to identify cases of misdeclaration and underpayment of taxes.
Field officers are instructed to issue formal show-cause notices and schedule personal hearings to allow importers to present their case regarding suspected discrepancies.
Customs Clearance: The process involves the submission of a Bill of Entry by an authorized clearing agent to facilitate the clearance of imported consignments.
Post-clearance audits may be conducted after the initial release of goods to ensure compliance with relevant laws and regulatory notifications.

Customs Act 1969: This clause provides a standardized template for issuing a demand notice regarding duties and taxes payable due to misdeclaration of goods during import as per the statutory provisions.
Sections 32(1), 32(2), and 32(4) of the Act establish the authority to demand duties, conduct show-cause proceedings, and determine the amount of short-paid customs duties.
Section 156 of the Act, specifically Table 1, Clause 14, outlines the penal consequences for misdeclaring the Harmonized System (HS) code during the import process.
Bangladesh Customs Tariff: This instrument is utilized by customs authorities during post-clearance audits to verify correct classification and duty assessment for imported goods.
World Customs Organization: The Explanatory Notes provided by this organization are referenced as authoritative guidance for the classification and assessment of goods during customs post-clearance audits.
Bill of Entry: The document is the primary record submitted by a customs clearing and forwarding agent to initiate the import clearance process for a specific shipment.
Customs Clearing and Forwarding Agent: These authorized agents are responsible for filing bills of entry on behalf of importers and must facilitate the payment of any assessed short-paid duties to the government treasury upon the issuance of a demand notice.

Customs Act 2023: The Act provides the legal basis for enforcing penalties regarding the misuse of duty and tax concessions through its specific penalty provisions.
Customs Offence Penalties: When an allegation of concession misuse is proven, the authority must recover the outstanding duties and taxes.
In addition to tax recovery, the authority must initiate proceedings against the offender based on the specific penalty item prescribed in the relevant schedule of the Customs Act.

Reassessment: This clause outlines the procedural requirements for the reassessment of goods, specifically when such reassessment necessitates the recovery of new or additional duties, taxes, or fees, or when refunds were granted in error.

The process requires documenting the grounds for reassessment and providing the concerned individual with formal notice according to the prescribed appendix, alongside an opportunity to respond in writing and attend a hearing within a specified timeframe.
Upon the expiration of the notice period, the reassessment must be finalized, and a formal demand notice must be issued according to the specified appendix.
Customs Act 1969: The reassessment process must be conducted in compliance with the requirements set forth in sub-section (3) of section 91 of the Customs Act 1969.
